bug_semantics: CVE-2026-73522 is a CWE-121 stack buffer overflow in Open1722's ACF-CAN example listener. avtp_to_can() in examples/acf-can/acf-can-common.c walks every ACF-CAN message in a received AVTP/UDP datagram and writes into can_frames[i++] with no capacity argument and no bound against MAX_CAN_FRAMES_IN_ACF (15). The Linux listener allocates a 15-slot stack array and the default stream ID 0xAABBCCDDEEFF0001 is hardcoded and unauthenticated on the wire, so an unauthenticated sender can put more than 15 valid ACF-CAN messages in one datagram and overflow adjacent stack (researcher ASan: 15 messages clean, 16 overflow at the payload memcpy). The same unbounded writer is reused by the Zephyr bridge. Distinct from CVE-2026-73523 (uint8_t truncation of a -1 return).
flaw_origin: The overflow did not exist in the original listener, which decoded into a single frame_t and wrote immediately to the CAN socket. It was first written in 67fd16fc27be8b5ae852229df743fff8558f4915 (2024-12-24, Naresh Nayak), which redesigned avtp_to_can() to fill a caller-supplied frame_t array, added #define MAX_CAN_FRAMES_IN_ACF 15, and had the Linux listener allocate frame_t can_frames[MAX_CAN_FRAMES_IN_ACF] without ever checking i. That commit is a distinct non-squash member of PR #62; the subject says 'refactored' but the unbounded array API and 15-slot stack buffer are new, not a move of a prior overflow. Parent 4412b5d9c371236cb66cb367da0c8c30faf15b27 still has void avtp_to_can(int eth_socket, int can_socket, ...) and no MAX_CAN_FRAMES_IN_ACF / can_frames[i++]. The unbounded increment survived through v0.8.0–v0.9.3 until PR #161.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-73522 is a published stack overflow, not a withdrawn advisory. The sink is avtp_to_can() incrementing a write index into a fixed 15-slot caller array with no capacity check, reachable from an unauthenticated UDP datagram whose only gate is a hardcoded stream ID. The original Open1722 listener (fbb88743, 2024-06-05) and the pre-67fd16fc avtp_to_can() used one frame_t and wrote to the CAN socket per message, so they could not overflow a 15-slot array. The smallest commit that first wrote the unbounded array mechanism is 67fd16fc27be8b5ae852229df743fff8558f4915; its parent 4412b5d9c371236cb66cb367da0c8c30faf15b27 was checked directly and lacks MAX_CAN_FRAMES_IN_ACF, can_frames[i++], and the 15-slot listener array. The commit message says refactor/platform split, but that is not a line-move of an existing overflow: the array-filling API and missing bound are new in this object, and PR #62 preserves it as a reconstructable member rather than a squash. Later commits (padding loop 5d7cf900, IsValid e85394e8) did not introduce the missing bound; valid >15-message datagrams still overflow through v0.9.2/v0.9.3. Fix 67443714946028a60afc06482e587d5b8b914a32 lands the bound check on main after those tags. AI judgment is BIC-only: Naresh Nayak at Bosch authored and committed 67fd16fc with a Signed-off-by trailer and no commit-object AI marker, so the real vulnerability is human-authored (NOT_AI). Copilot review on the later fix PR is irrelevant to BIC attribution.
